**Visual observations on test image:**
- Very small seedling (just post-emergence) collapsing at/near the soil line
- Cotyledons and hypocotyl are brown/tan, withered and collapsed
- Wet, dark moist soil surroundings
- No visible green tissue — completely brown and shriveled
- Soil appears to be sticking to the seedling tissue

**Key features aligning with candidates:**
- **Pythium damping-off**: Post-emergence collapse, brown rotted seedling at soil line, moist soil conditions — matches well
- **Rhizoctonia**: Dry, firm, reddish-brown sunken canker at soil line — the test seedling looks more collapsed/soft than a firm dry canker
- **Phytophthora**: Soft rot collapse in young plants — possible but usually involves more discoloration moving up the stem

**Comparison with Pythium reference:** The reference shows seedlings collapsing at soil level in wet/moist conditions with browning of hypocotyl/cotyledons — very similar setting and appearance to the test image. The test image represents a slightly more advanced stage (fully brown/collapsed), but the context matches well.

The wet soil environment and complete post-emergence collapse with brown rotted tissue at soil line is characteristic of Pythium damping-off.
